episode_title: 24 | How to Start Writing a Book: 4 Tips to Bring Your Idea to Life

real_qa.q: What is the key tip for determining when to stop writing and move into the editing phase of a book?
real_qa.r: Determine a cutoff point, which is essential whether you are writing a memoir or a novel. You need to establish a time frame for the setting—how many years, days, or hours the narrative will span. Without a clear cutoff point, the goalpost keeps moving as you continue learning and growing, making it impossible to transition from writing to editing. Create an anchor with a clear start and finish so you can focus your energy on that specific time period, give your brain structure, and maintain the stamina needed to complete the book.
real_qa.requete: book writing cutoff point editing phase

real_qa.q: How should you realistically integrate book writing into your existing schedule and life?
real_qa.r: Look at a typical week and count where you are actually spending your time—work, personal time, social activities—without rose-colored glasses. Understand where your brain is most creatively engaged for different phases of writing: for editing, many people are most fresh and focused in the morning; for initial creative writing, energy and schedule vary. Make the book fit into your actual life by being deliberate about prioritization; if the book does not logistically fit, it will never be prioritized and you will never find the time. Be realistic about what sacrifices or adjustments you need to make.
real_qa.requete: how to fit book writing into daily schedule

real_qa.q: What are effective physical triggers and reminders to spark creativity during book writing sessions?
real_qa.r: Create a physical reminder early on, such as a rough sketch or cover design of your book, which gives the book a face and helps you identify it as a creative entity. Print out your outline to have on your desk so you can mark it up with pen and paper. Create a physical trigger that alerts your brain you are entering writing mode—for example, lighting a specific lamp or lighting a scented candle that you only use when writing that particular book. The sensory trigger sends a message to your brain that it is time to write, helping you tap into the creative process more frequently without needing to wait for spontaneous inspiration.
real_qa.requete: physical triggers for creative writing productivity

real_qa.q: Why is remembering your initial commitment important when the book-writing process becomes difficult or non-linear?
real_qa.r: The book-writing process is not linear and often starts, stops, and continues, with periods of both progress and blankness. Remembering the yes you said to yourself and to the creative endeavor anchors you during these difficult phases. When you commit to a creative project, honor that sacred union with the idea, and you enter a state of co-creation where you feel more alive and awake to the world. Synchronicities happen more often, you notice things you would otherwise miss, and you feel part of something bigger than yourself. This co-creation, when you protect the space and take forward action, gives your life extra sparkle and makes the process feel like a beautiful partnership.
real_qa.requete: staying committed to writing a book when motivation drops

real_qa.q: How did Your 20s by Jess achieve consistent daily sales since its 2018 publication?
real_qa.r: Your 20s, published in 2018, has sold a copy somewhere around the world every single day since its publication, which Jess describes as rare, special, and mind-blowing. The book is a self-help book with self-discovery activities about navigating the ups and downs of your 20s. What makes it unique is that it was written by someone in their 20s, giving it a one-of-a-kind perspective, and it has withstood the test of time because it remains relevant, successful, and popular. However, Jess emphasizes that the key to the book's success is not about money; she does not focus on sales figures and recommends others not do so either, as the intrinsic fulfillment of completing and publishing a book is the true reward.
